decisions.reason: A flagship harvesting crate in a growing reusable agricultural packaging market keeps a valuable option open at low marginal cost, since the tooling is already sunk.
The foldable large container line had a dedicated page in both years, suggesting stable demand from automotive and industrial customers, so there is no evidence to justify abandoning it.
Stackable crates are a core, low-cost extension of the established portfolio, and keeping several models costs little while their value is still being realized.
Rackable pallets fit the firm's pallet range and pooling customers, and continued mention gives no signal that the option's value has collapsed.
Visibility dropped from its own page to a mention, a mild negative signal, but this niche spill-retention line is cheap to keep while demand uncertainty remains.
The single-model pallet lost its dedicated page, which suggests modest traction, yet its low holding cost means waiting for clearer results is preferable to dropping it now.
